note: Register a made-up person (use a test name and an address you control) on the live registration page, the way a real person would. Check three things: the person shows up in Contacts tagged as registered, the confirmation email arrives within a minute or two (look in junk too), and the event platform lists them. Delete the test registration afterwards. Why: it is the only way to know a real person will not meet a broken page.

stem: update the landing page to the new date
note: Change the date and time on the landing page and the registration form, then open the event platform (Zoom) and confirm it shows the same date and time. Check the registration button on the landing page opens the right form. Why: a mismatched date is the most common reason people miss a session.

stem: update the registration page to the new date
note: Change the date and time on the registration page and form, then open the event platform (Zoom) and confirm it shows the same date and time. Check the button opens the right form.

stem: update the social graphics, link-in-bio and short links
note: Swap every graphic that shows a date for the new one, change the link in your bio to the new registration page, and open each tracked short link (Short Links) to check it lands on the right page. Why: old dates and dead links send people to the wrong session.

stem: update the slides from the debrief
note: Open the last deck and apply what the debrief said: add answers to the questions people asked, tighten the sections where attention dropped, soften or sharpen the objections you heard, and update the date and the offer slide. Save it as this session's copy.

stem: send the invite email to your list
note: In Campaigns & Broadcasts > Broadcasts open the INVITE email for this date. Read it once, check the date, the registration link and the audience (it should skip people already registered), then approve and schedule or send it. Why: this is the first send that fills the room.

stem: personal invitations to your 20 warmest contacts
note: Pick the 20 people most likely to say yes: past clients, colleagues, people who have asked about your work. Message each one personally (not a copy and paste): say why you thought of them, give the date and their personal link. Log each one in your outreach pipeline. Aim for conversations, not blasts.

Send the share kit (copy, graphics and each person's own tracked link from Affiliates) to your partners, affiliates and past clients, with one personal line each. Using each person's own link means their registrations are credited to them.

In Campaigns & Broadcasts > Broadcasts open the TEACHING email for this date. Make sure your own story is filled in (no [brackets] left), check the date and link, then approve and confirm it is scheduled. Its job: teach one idea and invite.

Open the THIS WEEK email in Broadcasts, check the date and the join/registration link, and confirm it is scheduled for the morning of the week. Its job: remind people the session is days away and that a seat is still open.

Open the LAST CALL email in Broadcasts, check the time in every time zone and the link, and confirm it is scheduled for the day before. Its job: a short, warm final invitation, with the replay as the safety net.

stem: tech check and rehearse the offer
note: Do a 15-minute tech check in the real room: audio, camera, screen share, chat, recording and captions. Then say the offer out loud once, with the slides, and time it. Make sure there is one clear next step for everyone in the room and that its link works.

One post a day through the promotion window. About four in five give value (a lesson, a story, a question). About one in five is the invitation with the registration link. Draft and schedule them in the Content Calendar or Studio so the week is covered in one sitting.

stem: welcome dm to each new registrant
note: When someone registers, send them a short personal message the same day (the "Welcome, just registered" script for their platform, in Scripts). Ask what they most want to get clear on. Then press I sent it on their card so it is logged. This is the biggest lever for getting registrants into the room.

Send 25 new personal messages a day across LinkedIn, Instagram and Facebook from your Outreach Pipeline. Use the opener, then the invite after they reply or connect. Press I sent it on each card so the count and follow-ups are tracked.

Open MasterClass Results and compare registered against the goal. If you are under half of it, raise the DMs and the personal invitations this week and consider one more email or post. Write the number and what you changed in the project notes.

stem: confirm the reminder emails went out
note: In Campaigns & Broadcasts check the day-before and one-hour reminders show Sent. Decide who runs the chat and drops the links while you teach (you cannot do both) and tell that person what to post and when.

Open the room 15 minutes early, with recording and captions on. Welcome people as they arrive, teach, then give one clear next step for everyone in the room and drop its link in chat. Stay a few minutes after for questions.

After the session the attendance sync (every 15 minutes) tags who attended and who did not from the Zoom report. Open MasterClass Results > Registrations and fix anyone it missed. Why: the follow-up series branches on it.

stem: confirm the follow-up email series is running
note: In Campaigns check the ATTENDED and MISSED IT follow-up series show people enrolled, and that anyone who has already booked or enrolled is not still receiving emails.

stem: ask attendees for a one-line testimonial
note: Message the attendees who engaged with one question: what is one thing you took away? Use their words only with their permission and save the ones you can use in Testimonials.

72 hours after the replay went up, make the recording private or remove the link (Vimeo), and update the replay emails or page so the link does not dead-end. Why: the deadline is what makes people watch.
Open MasterClass Results: registered, attended, booked and sold, by channel. Write down what worked, what did not and what to change next time, in the project notes.

When the follow-up series has ended, anyone who did not book or enrol returns to your general list: remove the cycle's tags and make sure nobody is still stuck in a campaign. Then mark this project done.

stem: personal follow-up with the warmest attendees
note: Message the people who asked questions or stayed to the end: thank them, name one thing they said or asked, and offer the next step. Press I sent it on each one.
